response: The storm arrives on a wall of bruise-purple clouds, swallowing the afternoon sun in a single greedy gulp. A jagged vein of lightning fractures the sky, and seconds later the thunder rolls—a deep, bone-shaking growl that builds until it vibrates in your chest like a runaway freight train. The air shifts suddenly, charged with sharp, metallic ozone that prickles at the back of your throat, mixing with the rich, loamy scent of rain striking hot asphalt. Then the sky tears open. Drops fall heavy and cold, stinging exposed skin like thrown gravel, while the wind shoves against the trees in violent gusts, turning leaves silver-side-out in rolling waves. Between deafening claps of thunder, the temperature plummets, leaving gooseflesh on your arms as the rain drums against rooftops in a frenzied percussion that drowns out all thought.
